# The Mystery of Stablecoins, Visa, & Fiserv’s Collapse with Ken Suchoski | The Real Eisman Playbook

First listed: 2026-01-26 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The Mystery of Stablecoins, Visa, & Fiserv’s Collapse with Ken Suchoski | The Real Eisman Playbook](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z8rlpOF7vro) - 2026-01-26
- [Substack: The Mystery of Stablecoins, Visa, & Fiserv’s Collapse with Ken Suchoski | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 43](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-mystery-of-stablecoins-visa-and-9d5) - 2026-01-26

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Ken Suchoski explains stablecoin reserve economics, cross-border opportunities and the durable advantages of card networks. Eisman focuses on Tether contagion, consumer incentives and preference for Visa/Mastercard. Suchoski favors Circle after its valuation reset and Toast’s restaurant platform, while questioning Fiserv margins and the credit mix at Block. Later disclosures support Circle’s rate sensitivity and Fiserv margin pressure, but Circle’s token-presale revenue complicates apparent operating leverage. The review preserves the guest’s disagreement with Eisman about longer-run benefits from a hypothetical Tether scandal.

The strongest analysis concerns payment incentives, the distinction between rails and full services, and balance-and-yield economics. The Fiserv margin warning has substantial interim support. Weaknesses include overbroad claims that networks grow without paying distribution partners, insufficiently evidenced comparative compliance assertions, and valuation conclusions that need explicit price horizons. Many numerical examples are teaching illustrations and should not dominate the investment-thesis scorecard.

### 001. Fiat-backed stablecoins exchange customer dollars for tokens and invest backing assets, seeking a stable redemption value rather than Bitcoin-like price exposure.

**Right** | Ken Suchoski | material factual premise | supporting

[Source at 1:59-3:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z8rlpOF7vro&t=119s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Circle disclosures and the reserve framework support this description for reserve-backed payment stablecoins. It is not a guarantee of every token’s peg or a description of all algorithmic coins.

Qualification: A token tied to gold is stable in gold units, not necessarily in US dollars.

Assessment test: Establish whether the stated stablecoin reserve model proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.

- [Circle Q3 2026 Form 10-Q](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0001876042/b3ce97a8-6be6-4a55-bf46-b670adcb57f1.pdf) (2026-11-04): Reserve income fell 7.5%; a 61bp yield decline reduced it about $106.5m, partly offset by 8% average-USDC growth. ARC presale revenue of $181.8m materially boosted other revenue.
- [GENIUS Act, Public Law 119-27](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/COMPS-18221/pdf/COMPS-18221.pdf) (2025-07-18): Section 4 specifies eligible reserve assets, including short Treasuries, cash, deposits and qualifying repos/funds, along with reserve disclosures and examinations. Enactment is distinct from implementation dates and individual issuer compliance.

## Framework and tools

- Analyze both sides of a payment network, including consumer incentives rather than only merchant fees.
- Separate the settlement rail from compliance, local payout, distribution and workflow integration.
- Model Circle with reserve balances, yield and partner sharing rather than transaction volume alone.
